items.author: J. D. Salinger
items.desc: The book has a number of stories in it but my favorite is A Perfect Day for Bananafish which is just one of the best dialog heavy stories ever written.
items.title: A Perfect Day for Bananafish

items.author: J. D. Salinger
items.desc: Much like the movie Fight Club, there exist people who like this book for the wrong reasons. People who didn't understand that the main character is not meant to be someone you sympathize with.
items.title: The Catcher in the Rye

items.author: Frank Herbert
items.desc: I love the original trilogy of books for the deep lore, political intrigue, and plethora of fantastic ideas. You really have to read all three to understand what Herbert is doing and what Paul Muad'Dib represents.
items.title: Dune, Dune Messiah, Children of Dune

items.author: Frank Herbert
items.desc: My favorite Herbert book other than the Dune books. Very cool storyline and world building in this one. More relevant now than ever.
items.title: The Dosadi Experiment

items.author: Neil Gaiman
items.desc: I still love Sandman for what it did for comics despite Gaiman.
items.title: The Sandman

items.author: Clive Barker
items.desc: I think almost all of Barkers works are great but this one is by far my favorite. I love the way his prose is almost but not quiet poetry. Amazing world building and a strong character driven story.
items.title: Imajica

items.author: Octavia E. Butler
items.desc: I can't think of a more relevant book for our times. A cautionary tale that you must read.
items.title: Parable of the Sower

items.author: Jacqueline Carey
items.desc: This trilogy defines epic fantasy for me. Gruesome and raunchy. The main character is one of my favorites from any genre.
items.title: Kushiel's Dart, Kushiel's Chosen, Kushiel's Avatar

items.author: John Scalzi
items.desc: One of the few books ever that had me laughing out loud as I read it. Great sci-fi concepts and character driven stories. I recommend all books in this series.
items.title: Old Man's War

items.author: Scott Lynch
items.desc: A unique fantasy world, character driven plot, and fantastic set pieces and action scenes. I just adore these books. The second one in the series is my favorite.
items.title: The Lies of Locke Lamora

items.author: Iain M. Banks
items.desc: I recommend every single Culture book by Banks (except maybe Consider Phlebas) but Surface Detail is my favorite by a wide margin. Every book has great humor, strong characters, unpredictable and satisfying plots, and some of the coolest sci-fi concepts I've ever read.
items.title: Surface Detail

items.author: Ann Leckie
items.title: Ancillary Justice, Ancillary Sword, Ancillary Mercy

items.author: Ryan North
items.desc: My favorite comic book of all time. There's two volumes and I love both dearly. The premise is simple: What if King Midas's golden touch was real? Then years later a spaceship arrives intending to use his flesh as a weapon of mass destruction.
items.title: The Midas Flesh

items.author: Gemma Files
items.desc: My favorite horror novel. Won the Shirley Jackson Award for a reason. I don't want to spoil anything about it. Read it!
items.title: Experimental Film

items.author: N. K. Jemisin
items.title: The Fifth Season, The Obelisk Gate, The Stone Sky

items.author: V. E. Schwab
items.title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue

items.author: Derecka Purnell
items.title: Becoming Abolitionists: Police, Protests, and the Pursuit of Freedom
